impact: Driver unavailable for the whole day; their route must be split across other trucks, covered by a spare or dropped
note: BLS lost worktime rate for transportation and material moving occupations, 2025: 1.8% of usual hours (illness/injury 1.4, other 0.4) = probability a given driver-day is lost. Range 0.018-0.034: the absence rate (3.4%) counts anyone absent part of the reference week, so it is an upper bound per day. Industry (transportation and warehousing) lost worktime 1.7%.
source_name: BLS Current Population Survey, Table 47: Absences from work of employed full-time wage and salary workers by occupation and industry, 2025 annual averages

impact: Roadside breakdown; truck out of service for the rest of the day (impact duration not sourced, assumption)
note: Derived: 235.6 mi/day (FHWA VM-1 2023 combination 58,890 mi/yr / 250 days) / 23,769 truckload miles between breakdowns (Q2 2021) = 0.0099. Range 0.0057 (best-in-class TL 41,417 mi) to 0.0157 (Q1 2020 TL 14,991 mi).
source_name: Trucking Info (HDT), Fleet breakdown frequency improving (TMC/FleetNet America vertical roadside benchmarking, Q2 2021)

impact: Breakdown on a P&D route; remaining stops need a rescue truck
note: Derived: 46.4 mi/day (VM-1 2023 single-unit 11,593 mi/yr / 250 days) / 46,186 LTL miles between breakdowns (Q2 2021) = 0.0010. LTL figure pools linehaul and P&D; stop-start city duty is harder on equipment, so treat as a floor.
source_name: Trucking Info (HDT), Fleet breakdown frequency improving (TMC/FleetNet America vertical roadside benchmarking, Q2 2021)

impact: Breakdown mid-route; remaining stops need a rescue truck or roll to tomorrow
note: Derived: 46.4 mi/day single-unit / 23,769 mi between breakdowns (truckload vertical used as the less reliable proxy; no published local-delivery figure) = 0.0020. Range 0.0010 (LTL 46,186) to 0.0046 (2018 all-fleet ~10,000 mi between breakdowns, FleetOwner).
source_name: Trucking Info (HDT), Fleet breakdown frequency improving (TMC/FleetNet America vertical roadside benchmarking, Q2 2021)

impact: Breakdown on a dray; container misses its appointment or free-time window
note: Derived: 129 mi/day (CARB 2.4 moves x 53.8 mi loaded + bobtail) / 23,769 TL miles between breakdowns = 0.0054. Range to 0.0129 at the 2018 all-fleet ~10,000 mi.
source_name: Trucking Info (HDT), Fleet breakdown frequency improving (TMC/FleetNet America vertical roadside benchmarking, Q2 2021)

impact: Dwell runs past the 2 h free time; 1.4 h mean detention when it happens (VTTI 2014, cited); 30% of detained stops (9.9% of all) exceed 2 h of detention
note: Truckload dry van drivers: detention at 32.6% of stops in 2023. All sectors 39.3%; refrigerated 56.2%; flatbed 26.2%. Spot freight 42.5% vs contract 33.8%. LTL 'very little detention' (no number).
source_name: ATRI, Costs and Consequences of Truck Driver Detention (Sept 2024), 2023 data

impact: Load not ready at appointment; dwell runs past 2 h free time and the delivery appointment downstream is put at risk
note: Derived proxy: ATRI's 32.6% detention frequency covers pickups and deliveries together; not split. 57.8% of TL drivers were late to or cancelled a stop at least once in 2023 because of detention at the previous facility.
source_name: ATRI, Costs and Consequences of Truck Driver Detention (Sept 2024), 2023 data

impact: Stop fails; package returns on the truck, redelivery tomorrow
note: 100 - 99.22% US first-attempt delivery success (Q2 2025). High 0.028 = 100 - 97.2% (Parcel Monitor, via SmartRoutes). Most courier parcels can be left unattended; signature-required freight runs higher.
source_name: Parcel Perform, United States delivery performance Q2 2025

impact: Two-person crew arrives, nobody home; stop fails, crew time and truck slot lost, redelivery booked
note: 'The failure rate for first attempted home deliveries is 7.6%, but this rate more than doubles for the second and third attempted deliveries.' Attended delivery, Southeast Asian carrier data; no US bulky figure found.
source_name: Choo (2016), Impact of a Delivery Point Network (SUTD thesis; carrier data)

impact: That leg takes ~1.59x its typical congested time (+59%)
note: Derived: Planning Time Index is the 95th-percentile travel time ratio, so 1 peak trip in 20 runs at or beyond it. National average Oct-Dec 2025: PTI 2.03 vs Travel Time Index 1.28; 2.03 / 1.28 = 1.59. FHWA attributes ~25% of congestion to incidents (crashes, disabled vehicles) and 10% to work zones.
source_name: FHWA Urban Congestion Report, October-December 2025 (52 MSAs, NPMRDS)

impact: Arterial speeds down 10-25% on wet pavement (FHWA); freeway average speeds down 3-16% in rain
note: Derived: Minneapolis-St Paul normal 118.8 days/yr with precipitation >= 0.01 in / 365 = 0.325. One metro as stand-in; swap the station for another city. Speed impacts from FHWA Road Weather Management.
source_name: NOAA NCEI 2023 Local Climatological Data, Minneapolis-St Paul Intl Airport (1991-2020 normals)

impact: Arterial speeds down 30-40% on snowy/slushy pavement; freeway average speeds down 5-40% in heavy snow (FHWA)
note: Derived: Minneapolis-St Paul normal 14.6 days/yr with snowfall >= 1.0 in / 365 = 0.040 (concentrated Nov-Mar, ~3.3 days in Dec and Jan).
source_name: NOAA NCEI 2023 Local Climatological Data, Minneapolis-St Paul Intl Airport (1991-2020 normals)

impact: Shipment short, over or damaged (OS&D); claim, re-delivery or return
note: Proxy: Old Dominion 'cargo claims ratio below 0.1%' in Q4 2024. A claims ratio is claim dollars over revenue, not an incidence rate, and ODFL is the industry's best performer; a small carrier's exception rate is higher. Treat as a floor.
source_name: Old Dominion Freight Line Q4 2024 earnings release

probability_basis: per confirmed load (shipper-side cancellation, any time before pickup)
impact: Truck ordered not used: dispatched miles and the day's slot lost; TONU typically $150-$500 if collected at all
note: Faltings (2026), US spot-freight auction platform 2021-22, 563,620 shipments: 6.9% of confirmed shipments with no carrier cancellation were cancelled from the shipper side; 10.7% rescheduled. Shipper cancellations bunch 24-48 h before pickup, so only part of 6.9% hits a truck already rolling (TONU); treat as an upper bound. Carriers cancel 14.9% of confirmed shipments on the same platform (the reverse problem). TONU amounts are practitioner quotes from r/FreightBrokers (https://reddit.com/comments/1up4vhi).
source_name: Faltings, Pricing the Right to Renege in Search Markets: Evidence from Trucking (arXiv 2506.01650v2), Table 2

impact: A same-day order lands after routes are built; it must ride a route with slack, take a spare truck or roll to tomorrow. Typical failure: the add-on goes to a driver without the hours or the right equipment
note: No published or practitioner rate found; the scenario designer must set it. Voice only: 'Customer: 130pm - can you cover a small load? ... Shipper closes at 3pm. You have 90 MINUTES' (r/FreightBrokers, 2026-01-28); the add-on went out on a non-dock-high 26 ft van and the receiver demanded a price cut.
source_name: r/FreightBrokers, HOT last minute load delivered fine...we're upset!
